2026-09-07T03:01:29.6756406Z   pr_title: Orchestrator: post the remaining findings table when the security pass exhausts its fix-cycle budget
2026-09-07T03:01:29.6770287Z   pr_body: ## Summary

When the project security pass spends `MAX_SECURITY_PASS_CYCLES`, `security_pass_terminal_failure` posted only a count ("still reports N blocking finding(s)"), labelled the tracking issue `ai:security-pass-failed` and asked for manual intervention. The findings-JSON behind that count exists only in the runner's `RUNTIME_DIR`, so the operator asked to intervene had nothing to act on.

Trigger: shubhodeep1/tele-funtoken-msg-scoring#3928 exhausted cycle 3/3 on 2026-09-06 (`SECURITY_PASS_FAILED reason=cycle_exhausted ... cycles=3 findings=4` in consumer run 34049286004). The four findings were published nowhere: not the log, not the tracking comment, not the state-snapshot artifact. Each of the three earlier cycles did get a table, because `create_security_pass_fix_issue` renders one into the fix issue.

2026-09-06T11:51:31.7329450Z   pr_body: ## Summary

Project #3965 was terminalized as `ai:security-pass-failed` with a CRITICAL alert even though its security pass had already gone **clean**. A routine sync merge, not a code defect, triggered the failure.

Timeline reconstructed from the orchestrator state comments on #3965:

| Time (UTC) | `security_pass_status` | `security_pass_cycle` | Audited SHA |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 19:57 | `passed` | 3 | `75048a2c` |
| 20:03 | `running` | 3 | (cleared) |
| 20:13 | `failed` | 3 | `56f71c8f` |

`56f71c8f` is `chore: sync main into orchestrator/project-3965`, a merge commit that brought `main` into the integration branch. It advanced the head past the audited `75048a2c`, which invalidated the SHA-bound clean pass and forced a re-audit. The re-audit found 2 findings in the newly-arrived code, hit `completed_cycles >= MAX_SECURITY_PASS_CYCLES` on the very first check, and went straight to `security_pass_terminal_failure` with **zero** fix cycles spent on those findings.

## Root cause

`security_pass_cycle` is a lifetime counter. It is incremented only when a fix issue's PR merges, and reset only by `/re-security-pass` or by disabling the pass. Nothing resets it when an audit comes back clean.

But the counter's documented job is to bound *persistent* findings, which README describes as "consecutive fix cycles that failed to clear the same audit". A clean pass proves the loop converged and breaks that chain. Carrying the spent budget across a head advance means any project that needed all 3 cycles to reach clean is one sync merge away from a hard failure it can never work through on its own.

## The fix

`run_security_pass_inline` now resets `security_pass_cycle` to `0` when the prior status was `passed` and the current head no longer matches the audited SHA, loggin

2026-09-06T10:20:56.5181784Z   pr_body: ## Summary

Project #3965 was terminalized as `ai:security-pass-failed` with a CRITICAL alert even though its security pass had already gone **clean**. A routine sync merge, not a code defect, triggered the failure.

Timeline reconstructed from the orchestrator state comments on #3965:

| Time (UTC) | `security_pass_status` | `security_pass_cycle` | Audited SHA |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 19:57 | `passed` | 3 | `75048a2c` |
| 20:03 | `running` | 3 | (cleared) |
| 20:13 | `failed` | 3 | `56f71c8f` |

`56f71c8f` is `chore: sync main into orchestrator/project-3965`, a merge commit that brought `main` into the integration branch. It advanced the head past the audited `75048a2c`, which invalidated the SHA-bound clean pass and forced a re-audit. The re-audit found 2 findings in the newly-arrived code, hit `completed_cycles >= MAX_SECURITY_PASS_CYCLES` on the very first check, and went straight to `security_pass_terminal_failure` with **zero** fix cycles spent on those findings.

## Root cause

`security_pass_cycle` is a lifetime counter. It is incremented only when a fix issue's PR merges, and reset only by `/re-security-pass` or by disabling the pass. Nothing resets it when an audit comes back clean.

But the counter's documented job is to bound *persistent* findings, which README describes as "consecutive fix cycles that failed to clear the same audit". A clean pass proves the loop converged and breaks that chain. Carrying the spent budget across a head advance means any project that needed all 3 cycles to reach clean is one sync merge away from a hard failure it can never work through on its own.

2026-09-06T05:18:41.3687254Z   pr_title: fix(orchestrator): restore the security-fix budget when a clean pass is invalidated, and keep the tracking body honest on every security-pass transition
2026-09-06T05:18:41.3727678Z   pr_body: ## Summary

Project #3965 was terminalized as `ai:security-pass-failed` with a CRITICAL alert even though its security pass had already gone **clean**. A routine sync merge, not a code defect, triggered the failure.

Timeline reconstructed from the orchestrator state comments on #3965:

| Time (UTC) | `security_pass_status` | `security_pass_cycle` | Audited SHA |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 19:57 | `passed` | 3 | `75048a2c` |
| 20:03 | `running` | 3 | (cleared) |
| 20:13 | `failed` | 3 | `56f71c8f` |

`56f71c8f` is `chore: sync main into orchestrator/project-3965`, a merge commit that brought `main` into the integration branch. It advanced the head past the audited `75048a2c`, which invalidated the SHA-bound clean pass and forced a re-audit. The re-audit found 2 findings in the newly-arrived code, hit `completed_cycles >= MAX_SECURITY_PASS_CYCLES` on the very first check, and went straight to `security_pass_terminal_failure` with **zero** fix cycles spent on those findings.

## Root cause

`security_pass_cycle` is a lifetime counter. It is incremented only when a fix issue's PR merges, and reset only by `/re-security-pass` or by disabling the pass. Nothing resets it when an audit comes back clean.

But the counter's documented job is to bound *persistent* findings, which README describes as "consecutive fix cycles that failed to clear the same audit". A clean pass proves the loop converged and breaks that chain. Carrying the spent budget across a head advance means any project that needed all 3 cycles to reach clean is one sync merge away from a hard failure it can never work through on its own.

## The fix

`run_security_pass_inline` now resets `security_pass_cycle` to `0` when the prior status was `passed` and the current head no longer matches the audited SHA, loggin
